Q77 • Short Answer Circuit Components & Symbols
Medium 3 Marks
Why is a switch placed anywhere in a circuit able to control the bulb?
Model Textbook Solution
An electric current requires an unbroken, closed conducting loop to flow from the positive terminal to the negative terminal of the cell. If the switch is opened (OFF) atany pointin the circuit, the conductive loop is broken (open circuit), halting the flow of electrons through all components immediately.
Examiner & Concept Tip: Official NCERT textbook diagrammatic solution.
Q78 • Short Answer Circuit Components & Symbols
Medium 3 Marks
Explain why the filament of an electric bulb glows white-hot while the connecting wires remain cool.
Model Textbook Solution
The filament is fabricated fromtungsten, which possesses extremely high electrical resistance and an ultra-high melting point (approx. 3422°C). When current passes through, the high resistance causes intense Joule heating (H = I²Rt), heating it to white incandescence (~2500°C) to emit visible light.In contrast, connecting wires are composed of thickcopper or aluminiumwith negligible electrical resistance, so heat dissipation is imperceptibly small.
Examiner & Concept Tip: Official NCERT textbook diagrammatic solution.
Q79 • Short Answer Circuit Components & Symbols
Medium 3 Marks
Name two devices that deliberately utilize the heating effect of electric current, and state the material used for their heating elements.
Model Textbook Solution
Devices:Electric iron, electric toaster, geyser, room heater.Material:Nichrome(an alloy of nickel, chromium, and iron) because of its exceptionally high resistivity and high resistance to oxidation (does not burn or melt easily at high temperatures).
Examiner & Concept Tip: Official NCERT textbook diagrammatic solution.
Q80 • Short Answer Circuit Components & Symbols
Medium 3 Marks
Explain the working principle and construction of an electric fuse. Why should a thick copper wire never be used as a fuse wire?
Model Textbook Solution
An electric fuse is a critical safety device designed to break the circuit in the event of excessive current (overloading or short-circuiting). It consists of a thin alloy wire (typically tin-lead alloy) with alow melting point.When current exceeds the safe limit, the Joule heat generated (I²Rt) rapidly raises the temperature past the alloy's melting point, causing the wire to melt and break the circuit safely.Why copper wire must NOT be used:Copper has very low resistance and a very high melting point (1085°C). It will not melt during dangerous current spikes, allowing the excessive current to overheat house wiring and cause catastrophic electrical fires.
Examiner & Concept Tip: Official NCERT textbook diagrammatic solution.
Q81 • Short Answer Circuit Components & Symbols
Medium 3 Marks
What is a Miniature Circuit Breaker (MCB), and what advantage does it offer over traditional wire fuses?
Model Textbook Solution
AnMCBis an automatic electromagnetic switch that automatically trips into the 'OFF' position whenever current exceeds safe thresholds. Unlike traditional fuses that require manual replacement of melted wires, an MCB can be simply reset back to the 'ON' position once the electrical fault is corrected.
Examiner & Concept Tip: Official NCERT textbook diagrammatic solution.
Q82 • Short Answer Circuit Components & Symbols
Medium 3 Marks
Describe Oersted's experiment and state its fundamental scientific conclusion.
Model Textbook Solution
In 1820, Danish scientist Hans Christian Oersted placed a magnetic compass needle parallel and close to a straight conducting wire. When electric current was switched ON, the compass needle immediately deflected from its North-South alignment. When the current was reversed, the needle deflected in the opposite direction. When current was switched OFF, the needle returned to magnetic North.Conclusion:An electric current flowing through a conductor generates a surroundingmagnetic field.
Examiner & Concept Tip: Official NCERT textbook diagrammatic solution.
Q83 • Short Answer Circuit Components & Symbols
Medium 3 Marks
Explain the working mechanism of an electric bell with a circuit schematic description.
Model Textbook Solution
An electric bell operates via an electromagnet and a make-and-break contact mechanism:When the bell switch is pressed, current flows through the electromagnet coil, magnetizing its soft iron core.The energized electromagnet attracts the soft iron armature attached to a spring strip.As the armature rushes toward the electromagnet, the striker hits the metallic gong, producing a loud ring.However, this forward motion simultaneously pulls the contact screw away from the contact strip, breaking the circuit.With the circuit broken, current stops, the electromagnet de-energizes, and the spring pulls the armature back.As the armature springs back, it touches the contact screw again, completing the circuit once more. This rapid make-and-break cycle repeats continuously as long as the switch is held down.
Examiner & Concept Tip: Official NCERT textbook diagrammatic solution.
Q84 • Short Answer Circuit Components & Symbols
Medium 3 Marks
HOTS Q1: Four identical bulbs A, B, C, and D are connected in a circuit. Bulbs A and B are in series, and this combination is connected in parallel with bulb C. Bulb D is connected in the main line. If bulb C's filament breaks, explain what happens to the brightness of bulbs A, B, and D.
Model Textbook Solution
Circuit Analysis:Total circuit current flows through main-line bulb D before splitting into parallel branches (A+B) and C.When bulb C burns out, branch C becomes an open circuit.The total equivalent resistance of the entire circuit increases because the parallel path has been removed.Due to the increased total resistance, the total current drawn from the battery decreases. Hence, bulb D in the main line dims slightly.However, the voltage across the surviving branch (A+B) increases because the voltage drop across D has decreased. Therefore, bulbs A and B actually glow brighter than before!
Examiner & Concept Tip: Official NCERT textbook diagrammatic solution.
Q85 • Short Answer Circuit Components & Symbols
Medium 3 Marks
HOTS Q2: Why are LEDs (Light Emitting Diodes) increasingly replacing incandescent bulbs and CFLs? State two major technical advantages.
Model Textbook Solution
Advantages of LEDs:High Energy Efficiency:LEDs produce light via electroluminescence (electron-hole recombination in semiconductors) without wasting massive energy as heat (>80% less energy consumed than incandescent bulbs).Long Lifespan & Durability:LEDs have no fragile filament to break or burn out, operating for 25,000 to 50,000 hours with negligible heat dissipation.
Examiner & Concept Tip: Official NCERT textbook diagrammatic solution.

A fuse must melt before copper conducting wires can overheat, so it is made of an alloy (tin-lead) with a specifically low melting point.
Fill in Blank #15 1 Mark
Doctors use very small but strong _______ to remove iron dust or magnetic splinters from a patient's eye.
Answer: electromagnets
Miniature electromagnets generate focused magnetic fields that attract ferromagnetic particles safely out of ocular tissue without mechanical cuts.
Fill in Blank #16 1 Mark
If the amount of current passing through the coil of an electromagnet is decreased, the strength of the electromagnet will _______.
Answer: decrease
The magnetic field strength B of an electromagnet is directly proportional to the current (I) circulating in its coil turns.
Fill in Blank #17 1 Mark
A battery, made up of more than one cell in series, is used to provide _______ current in the circuit than a single cell.
Answer: greater (higher)
Connecting cells in series adds their electromotive forces (V_total = V₁ + V₂ + ...), driving greater current through a given circuit resistance (I = V / R).
Fill in Blank #18 1 Mark
Electric current flows where there is some difference in _______.
Answer: electric potential (potential difference / voltage)
Charges flow along a conductor only when an electric potential gradient exists between two points, driving electrons from low to high potential.

State True or False: An insulator does not allow electric current to pass through it.

Insulators lack free valence electrons, presenting extremely high electrical resistance and preventing current flow.
True / False #2 Unanswered

Scientific Rationale:
A switch is convenient for control, but current will flow in any continuous unbroken conducting loop between cell terminals, even without an intervening switch.

State True or False: A lamp with a broken filament is a fused lamp.

A bulb is termed 'fused' when its tungsten filament wire melts or snaps, breaking the internal circuit path.

State True or False: An electric switch in 'OFF' position eases the flow of electric current.

True / False #6 Unanswered
State True or False: To make a battery of two cells, the negative terminal of one cell is connected to the negative terminal of the other cell.
Scientific Rationale:
To connect cells in series to form a battery, the negative terminal of the first cell must connect to the positive terminal of the next cell.
True / False #7 Unanswered
State True or False: When the electric current through a fuse exceeds a certain limit, the fuse wire melts and breaks.
Scientific Rationale:
Excessive current generates heat above the alloy's low melting point, causing the fuse wire to melt and disconnect the circuit.

State True or False: An electromagnet does not attract a piece of iron.
Scientific Rationale:
When energized, an electromagnet generates a strong magnetic field that strongly attracts ferromagnetic materials like iron.
True / False #9 Unanswered
State True or False: An electric bell has an electromagnet.
Scientific Rationale:
The core functioning of an electric bell relies on an electromagnet to pull an iron armature and strike a gong repeatedly.

State True or False: An MCB can be used instead of a fuse in an electrical circuit.

True / False #11 Unanswered
State True or False: Connecting two cells negative-to-negative will double the voltage of the battery.
Scientific Rationale:
Opposing like terminals (− to −) cancel out cell voltages, reducing net potential difference to zero instead of doubling it.

State True or False: The melting of a fuse wire is an application of the magnetic effect of electric current.

Fuse wire melting is an application of the heating effect of electric current (Joule heating, H = I²Rt), not the magnetic effect.

State True or False: Tungsten is selected for bulb filaments because it has an extremely low melting point.

True / False #15 Unanswered

Assertion: A battery is used to power an electrical circuit.
Reason: A battery provides a source of voltage (potential difference) to move electrons through the circuit.
Official Solution (A):
A battery maintains a potential difference between its terminals, which exerts an electric force that drives free electrons through the conducting circuit loop.
Assertion & Reason #2 Unanswered
Directions: Mark (a) if both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation; (b) if both are true but reason is not the correct explanation; (c) if assertion is true but reason is false; (d) if assertion is false but reason is true.

Assertion: The switch in a circuit is used to control the flow of electricity.
Reason: The switch opens or closes the circuit loop to either allow or stop the flow of current.
Official Solution (A):
Closing the switch establishes conducting continuity; opening the switch introduces an air gap, arresting the flow of current.
Assertion & Reason #3 Unanswered
Directions: Mark (a) if both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation; (b) if both are true but reason is not the correct explanation; (c) if assertion is true but reason is false; (d) if assertion is false but reason is true.

Assertion: An electric switch is not a necessary component of electric circuits, so it must be avoided in circuits to save electricity.
Reason: An electric switch is used to make or break the circuit whenever required.
Official Solution (D):
The assertion is false: switches are crucial for safety, appliance life, and energy conservation. The reason is a true statement describing the switch's operating function.
Assertion & Reason #4 Unanswered
Directions: Mark (a) if both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation; (b) if both are true but reason is not the correct explanation; (c) if assertion is true but reason is false; (d) if assertion is false but reason is true.

Assertion: Fuses are used in electric circuits of buildings.
Reason: A fuse prevents electrical fires and damage to appliances caused by excessive flow of current.
Official Solution (A):
Fuses are standard safety requirements in building circuits because their sacrificial melting interrupts hazardous fault currents before they cause fires.
Assertion & Reason #5 Unanswered
Directions: Mark (a) if both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation; (b) if both are true but reason is not the correct explanation; (c) if assertion is true but reason is false; (d) if assertion is false but reason is true.

Assertion: Copper wires are used for making connections in a circuit as they are good conductors of electric current.
Reason: When current passes through the copper wire, it behaves like a magnet.
Official Solution (B):
Both statements are factually true. However, copper is chosen for wiring because of its very low electrical resistivity, high ductility, and cost-effectiveness, not because it produces a magnetic field.
Assertion & Reason #6 Unanswered
Directions: Mark (a) if both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation; (b) if both are true but reason is not the correct explanation; (c) if assertion is true but reason is false; (d) if assertion is false but reason is true.

Assertion: The amount of heat produced in a wire depends on its material, length, and thickness.
Reason: If a small normal current passes through the filament of an electric bulb, the filament becomes so hot that it melts and breaks.
Official Solution (C):
The assertion is true (H depends on R = ρl/A). The reason is false because a normal operating current heats the tungsten filament to a stable incandescent glow without melting it; tungsten melts only at 3422°C.
Assertion & Reason #7 Unanswered
Directions: Mark (a) if both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation; (b) if both are true but reason is not the correct explanation; (c) if assertion is true but reason is false; (d) if assertion is false but reason is true.

Assertion: The strength of an electromagnet can be increased by increasing the number of turns of the coil.
Reason: A soft iron piece kept inside a current-carrying coil behaves like a magnet when electricity is passed through the wire.
Official Solution (B):
Both statements are true. However, increasing turns increases strength because each turn adds an incremental magnetic field loop (B ∝ n), whereas the reason simply explains that soft iron acts as a magnetic core.
Assertion & Reason #8 Unanswered
Directions: Mark (a) if both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation; (b) if both are true but reason is not the correct explanation; (c) if assertion is true but reason is false; (d) if assertion is false but reason is true.

Assertion: Soft iron is used for making electromagnets.
Reason: Soft iron loses all its magnetism quickly when current is switched off.
Official Solution (A):
Soft iron is the ideal core for temporary electromagnets precisely because of its low retentivity: it magnetizes intensely when current flows and demagnetizes promptly when current stops.

High-Stakes Exam Defense

Exam Traps, 16 3D Flashcards & Video Vault

Avoid the 8 classic misconceptions where students lose marks, plus 16 interactive flip cards and curated lectures.

!

The 8 Fatal Exam Traps in Electricity

Trap 1: Battery Series Connection
Wrong: Connecting (+) to (+) or (-) to (-) in a battery

Correct: In series, (+) of one cell must connect to (-) of the next! If connected (+) to (+), voltages oppose each other (net 0V) and bulb never glows.

Trap 2: Meaning of a "Fused" Bulb
Wrong: Bulb is broken on the outside glass

Correct: The delicate tungsten filament inside is snapped! This creates an internal open circuit, halting current everywhere.

Trap 3: Current in an Open Circuit
Wrong: Current reaches up to the open switch and stops there

Correct: Electric current is a continuous loop! If a switch is OFF anywhere, current is zero throughout the entire circuit simultaneously.

Trap 4: Fuse Wire Material Mistake
Wrong: Replacing a burnt fuse with thick copper wire

Correct: Copper has a high melting point (1085°C)! It will NOT melt during surges, defeating the safety purpose and causing fires.

Trap 5: Heater Element vs Bulb Filament
Wrong: Electric iron heating element is made of tungsten

Correct: Heating elements use Nichrome alloy (high resistance, no oxidation in air). Bulb filaments use Tungsten (extremely high melting point 3422°C).

Trap 6: Magnetic Deflection with Reversed Current
Wrong: Compass needle always deflects to the east

Correct: If you reverse the terminals of the battery, the compass needle deflects in the opposite direction!

Trap 7: Electromagnet Core Material
Wrong: Using a steel nail for an electromagnet

Correct: Steel retains permanent magnetism and cannot be switched off! Electromagnets require soft iron cores for instant demagnetization.

Trap 8: Electric Bell Contact Screw Action
Wrong: Current flows continuously while the bell is ringing

Correct: When the hammer hits the gong, contact with the screw breaks, cutting off current. The circuit is continuously made and broken dozens of times per second!
